gen-fs-styro-gf-onest: Retro and tightly packed, Styro crowds its letters together while Onest spreads out with short ascenders and big, generous bowls. Its curves never thin out.
gen-fs-styro-gf-orienta: Orienta reads modern and unfussy, with open counters and capitals that barely tower over the lowercase. Styro does its best work crammed and commanding, while Orienta does its best work breathing.
gen-fs-styro-gf-oxygen: Clean and contemporary, Oxygen leaves its curves open and keeps the lowercase nearly level with the capitals. Next to Styro's crowded, closed-up letters, it feels like stepping outside.
gen-fs-styro-gf-parkinsans: Parkinsans reads crisp and modern, with wide-mouthed letters that hold up small. Styro brings a retro, commanding crowding of letters, while Parkinsans never flickers between thick and thin.
gen-fs-styro-gf-pathway-extreme: Styro packs its letters so tight they nearly touch. Its commanding bulk is the strength here, and Pathway Extreme answers with clear openings, stubby ascenders and a big x-height.
gen-fs-styro-gf-preahvihear: Contemporary and open, this pairing sets Styro's crowded, closed letters against something airier. Preahvihear opens its letter mouths like a pried oyster shell, and its lofty x-height keeps a long read from feeling heavy.
gen-fs-styro-gf-pt-sans-caption: Styro is retro and commanding, with its lowercase pressed tight and its e and c almost shut. PT Sans Caption does the opposite job well, leaving its bowls unclosed and inviting on big-bodied lowercase.
gen-fs-styro-gf-puritan: Approachable Puritan keeps its rounded forms open to the side, with oversized e and a counters. And Styro, retro and crowded, gives the page its closed, commanding voice while Puritan lets the text breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-questrial: Questrial brings open s shapes and a flat, stencil-cut feel from strokes that never swell on the downstrokes. But Styro is the one that commands, with its crowded retro lowercase, while Questrial stays level and tall.
gen-fs-styro-gf-radio-canada: Professional and steady, Radio Canada draws its tall c, s and z like bent wire. Styro keeps its crowded retro grip on the headings, so the body text can go slightly larger without losing that open feel.
